messages:
marta: Heads up — seeing intermittent packet drops on the overlay (vxlan) between gpu-nodes in eu-west-1. Started during a backfill around 14:12. Jobs show allreduce stalls. Anyone else?
lee: yeah I noticed retries in the training queue too. do you have a quick capture? :eyes: 
jordan: if host pcap vs pod pcap differ it's often offload / encap egress issues. are we running RDMA on those pools?
marta: RDMA is enabled for the pool. Quick notes: host tcpdump (on the egress leaf) shows UDP vxlan retransmits + ICMP frag needed sometimes. Pod-level pcap inside container sees fewer drops. cpu/gpu utilization looked fine.
lee: that host-vs-pod difference is telling — GRO/GSO/TCO could be folding packets so pod sees reassembled stream while host sees encap issues. Can you paste ethtool -k and ip link output?
marta: paste: ```
$ ip link show dev vxlan0
5: vxlan0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UP mode DEFAULT group default 
    link/ether 3a:ff:12:aa:bb:cc brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
$ ethtool -k vxlan0 | egrep -i "gso|gro|tso"
GSO: on
GRO: on
TSO: on
```
marta: iperf3 between hosts shows latency spikes every ~15-25s coinciding with ~0.5-2% packet loss reported by jobs.
jordan: try toggling gro/gso on the vxlan device on one node to repro: 
```bash
for f in vxlan0; do sudo ethtool -K $f gro off gso off tso off; done
```
jordan: disable on one side and run the backfill to see if drops go away.
tess: we did a quick toggle in a canary: turning GRO off on the vxlan iface reduced visible packet loss in host captures to near 0, but CPU went up ~6%. Jobs stopped triggering redispatch. So it's linked to offload path.
lee: do we have any node provisioning events? i.e. new nodes with different kernel/firmware? sometimes cloud-init changes bridge mtu or misses vxlan mtu bump.
marta: yes — two nodes spun up at 14:12 from the autoscaler with the new image. their cloud-init log shows missing mtu tweak for br0. suspect: encap increases packet size above path MTU and offload + fragmentation interacts badly with NIC driver.
jordan: that fits. If encapsulated packet > underlying MTU and offload happens post-encap, checksums/GSO reassembly may be wrong. Which NIC driver? mlx5?
marta: mlx5_core on these nodes, driver version 5.12.x.
lee: short plan: 1) roll back autoscaler to avoid new nodes (pin image), 2) schedule controlled repro with gro off/on, 3) collect host pcap and pod pcap simultaneously (tcpdump -w host.pcap and nsenter for pod), 4) open vendor ticket with captures and kernel logs.
tess: also try net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 and set vxlan mtu explicitly to (underlay_mtu - 50) in cloud-init for next boot.
marta: created a small capture on both host and pod and uploaded to S3: s3://rwd-infra-debug/1762509876/pcap-host.pcap & pcap-pod.pcap.
lee: temporary mitigation: disabling GRO on vxlan as a daemonset for affected pool (we should be careful on CPU) or set instance pool to older image without rmda/driver mismatch.
jordan: +1 on vendor ticket. also check sysctl net/ipv4/conf/*/rp_filter? sometimes weird pathing with multiple routes.
sre-bot: incident created: INF-17625-overlay-flicker — assigned to eng-infra oncall.
marta: I'll do the canary repro and post logs. keeping autoscaler pinned for now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
